meta.reader: a provider-operations lead who has never seen the codebase
meta.contradicts: that running hundreds of company sites means running hundreds of copies of the program

sections.asks: Why one program instead of one copy per company?
sections.shows: the familiar thing on the left and the subject on the right, the same layout twice with different nouns

sections.asks: How many programs are actually running?
sections.shows: a column of typed addresses on the left, lines converging into a single box on the right holding the numeral one

instead_of.because: a sankey would give the lines a width and there is no quantity flowing along them, only the fact that they all end in the same place

sections.asks: How does one program know whose site to show?
sections.shows: one picture drawn twice, gaining the piece that does the choosing on the second pass

sections.asks: Who answers when everyone arrives at once?
sections.shows: three layers, the outermost taking most of the arrivals and the innermost taking the fewest

sections.asks: What happens between typing an address and seeing a page?
sections.shows: the steps in order along one line, from the address bar to the rendered page

sections.asks: How is a new company's site switched on?
sections.shows: one lane per party, the work handing across between them in time order

sections.asks: What is the site never allowed to do?
sections.shows: what a site may do and what it may not, each line marked, the boundary between them visible at a glance
